name: Oliver Hazard Perry-class frigate (long hull)
className: Oliver Hazard Perry class (FFG 7), long-hull variant
role: Guided-missile frigate for convoy escort, anti-submarine warfare and local air defense, with two SH-60B helicopters

serviceWindow.statusNotes: USS Taylor was commissioned on 1 December 1984 and decommissioned on 8 May 2015. The US Navy retired its Perry-class frigates by 2015. The class did not end there: other navies still operate Perry-class ships, including Turkey, Egypt, Poland, Pakistan, Spain, Taiwan, Bahrain and Chile, and Taylor herself went to Taiwan (now ROCS Ming Chuan, PFG-1112). Taylor served in the Gulf region in 1988 and 1990. In the 2026 scenario this is a legacy US hull kept as a historical stand-in, not a ship the US Navy fields today.

dimensions.crew: About 176 (Wikipedia); FAS gives about 15 officers and 179 enlisted. Plus the aviation detachment for two SH-60B helicopters. Displacement is in long tons.

propulsionSummary: Two General Electric LM2500 gas turbines, about 41,000 shaft horsepower together, drive a single propeller shaft.

weapons.name: RIM-66 SM-1MR
weapons.mountSummary: Mk 13 Mod 4 single-arm launcher with a 40-round magazine shared with Harpoon (36 Standard Missile and 4 Harpoon)

weapons.name: Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS
weapons.mountSummary: One Mk 15 close-in weapon system mount; the quantity is rounds of 20 mm ammunition

sensors.name: AN/SPS-49(V) air search radar
sensors.role: Long-range two-dimensional air search; the main early-warning sensor. The published maximum instrumented range of the A(V)1 version is 474 km, but the engine uses a shorter practical figure.

sensors.name: AN/SPS-55 surface search radar
sensors.role: Surface search and navigation: finds ships, small boats and low aircraft

sensors.name: AN/SLQ-32(V)2 electronic support system
sensors.role: Passive warning receiver that picks up hostile radar emissions and gives bearings. Its antennas sit low on the ship, which limits intercept range to about 23 nautical miles.

sensors.name: AN/SQS-56 hull-mounted sonar
sensors.role: Active and passive search for submarines near the ship; the AN/SQR-19 towed array adds longer-range passive listening. No public detection range found, so this is an open estimate.

radar.note: A 4,100-ton steel hull with an unshaped superstructure; it shows up clearly to search radar but is smaller than a destroyer or cruiser.

infrared.note: Two gas turbines put out a hot exhaust plume, and no special infrared suppression is described in the sources.

acoustic.note: Gas turbines on a single shaft; it is not a quiet platform for a submarine to listen to, and it tows its own array to hear them first.

visual.note: A 138 m ship is easy to see at sea in daylight.

brief.whatItIs: The Oliver Hazard Perry class was the US Navy's mass-produced guided-missile frigate from the late 1970s. The long-hull version, such as USS Taylor, is 138 m long and carries two SH-60B helicopters in a hangar. It was built to escort convoys and carrier groups against submarines and aircraft at a low cost per ship.
brief.howItIsUsed: A commander uses a Perry as a picket and escort. The SPS-49 radar watches the air picture, the sonar and towed array listen for submarines, and the two SH-60B helicopters extend the ship's reach out past the horizon in both anti-submarine and surface search. The single Mk 13 launcher holds 36 SM-1 Standard missiles and 4 Harpoon missiles in one shared magazine, so it can fire only one missile at a time and the load runs out fast against a big raid. The Phalanx gun is the last-ditch defense against sea-skimming missiles. Keep it inside a larger group's air cover when facing heavy air threats. Its low-mounted ESM and limited missile magazine are the weak points.
typicalMissions: Escort a convoy or a high-value ship through a choke point
Anti-submarine screen with towed array and helicopters
Local air defense with SM-1MR and Phalanx
